messages.content:
You turn prior-authorization documentation gaps into concrete tasks for a care team.

For each gap you get the coverage criterion, the policy text it comes from, and why it is not yet proven (the evidence reviewer's finding, or a payer objection the provider could not answer). Write one task per gap:
- `title`: imperative and specific, under 100 characters ("Document PT start/end dates and outcome").
- `detail`: what exactly to add to the chart and why, quoting the policy requirement. 1–3 sentences.
- `assignee_role`: `clinician` if it needs clinical documentation or an exam; `coordinator` if it is a records request or administrative.

Do not invent clinical facts or say the patient qualifies. Return one task for every gap key given, using the same `criterion_key`.

criterion_key: sev.baseline
criterion: Objective pain scale or functional assessment recorded at baseline
policy (L39240): An objective pain scale or functional assessment must be performed at baseline (prior to interventions)
why not proven: quote does not entail the claim (p=0.01)

criterion_key: contra
criterion: No contraindication (spinal or systemic infection, cord/conus/cauda equina compression, cancer risk)
policy (L39240): suspected or active localized spinal infection, significant systemic infection, compressive lesions of the spinal cord, conus medullaris or cauda equina, suspicion or major risk factors for cancer
why not proven: There is no documentation in the chart excerpts that addresses the presence or absence of contraindications (infection, compression, or cancer risk) as required by the criterion. No relevant findings are described in the available notes or reports.

criterion_key: dx.radic
criterion: Radiculopathy, radicular pain or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte or severe DDD producing foraminal or central stenosis
policy (L39240): Lumbar, cervical or thoracic radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication due to disc herniation, osteophyte or osteophyte complexes, severe degenerative disc disease, producing foraminal or central spinal stenosis
why not proven: Payer objection (medium): The cited MRI quote notes 'moderate right foraminal stenosis contacting the exiting nerve root.' Mere contact with the nerve root, without documented compression or displacement, may not sufficiently establish that the disc herniation is the definitive cause producing the radiculopathy. Provider response: The chart excerpts document radiculopathy and MRI findings of foraminal stenosis contacting the nerve root, but do not explicitly state nerve root compression or displacement. Documentation directly describing compression or displacement is missing.

response: {"tasks":[{"criterion_key":"sev.baseline","title":"Document objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline","detail":"Add documentation of an objective pain scale or functional assessment performed prior to interventions, as required by policy L39240: 'An objective pain scale or functional assessment must be performed at baseline (prior to interventions).'","assignee_role":"clinician"},{"criterion_key":"contra","title":"Document absence or presence of contraindications","detail":"Add clinical documentation addressing the presence or absence of contraindications such as spinal or systemic infection, cord/conus/cauda equina compression, or cancer risk, per policy L39240 requirements.","assignee_role":"clinician"},{"criterion_key":"dx.radic","title":"Document nerve root compression or displacement causing radiculopathy","detail":"Add clinical or imaging documentation explicitly stating nerve root compression or displacement caused by disc herniation, osteophyte, or severe degenerative disc disease producing foraminal or central stenosis, as required by policy L39240.","assignee_role":"clinician"}]}
